1: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' faith, love and hope. They received the word with joy in spite of suffering, turned from idols to the living God, and their example has spread everywhere.
This is probably the oldest writing in the New Testament. Conversion means turning from idols to serve the true God.
2: Paul reminds them he did not flatter or seek money. He was gentle among them like a nursing mother and encouraged them like a father. They received his preaching as what it really is, the word of God.
The apostles' preaching carries God's own word. Good ministry shares life, not only information.
3: Unable to bear not knowing, Paul sent Timothy to see how they were coping with persecution. Timothy reports that they stand firm. Paul prays that their love may increase.
Paul's joy is tied to the faith of the people he taught. Christians are to strengthen one another under trial.
4: Holiness and hope for the dead

God's will is that you be holy: keep away from sexual immorality and love one another. About those who have died, do not grieve like people without hope. The Lord will come, the dead in Christ will rise, and we will be with the Lord always.
Christians do grieve, but with hope. Death does not break our union with Christ.
5: That day will come like a thief in the night, so stay awake and sober. Respect your leaders, be patient with everyone, rejoice always, pray constantly, give thanks in all circumstances, and test everything.
We do not know the date, so we live ready. "Pray without ceasing" describes a whole way of life.
